en.title: Halo Multiplayer Project 'Ekur' Reportedly Canceled by 343 Industries
en.summary: A promising new multiplayer-only Halo game, codenamed 'Ekur,' has reportedly been scrapped. This cancellation leaves fans questioning the future of large-scale Halo combat experiences.
en.body:
The Halo universe is once again facing uncertainty as reports suggest that a new multiplayer-focused project, codenamed **Project Ekur**, has been canceled. This ambitious undertaking was reportedly being developed by **Certain Affinity**, a studio with a long history of supporting major franchises like Halo and Call of Duty. The news, initially broken by Halo insider **Rebs Gaming** and corroborated by sources like **Jez Corden** of Windows Central, indicates that the project is no longer in development.

**Project Ekur** was envisioned as a significant expansion of Halo's multiplayer offerings, drawing inspiration from beloved modes like **Halo 5's Warzone**. It was described as a "super big team battle idea," aiming to deliver large-scale engagements that have long been a staple of the franchise. The project was reportedly built upon the foundation of an earlier scrapped battle royale-style game, **Project Tatanka**, and was being developed using the Unreal Engine. Early concepts even included customizable Spartans and Elites, hinting at a deep level of player personalization that would have been a welcome addition for many fans. The exact reasons for the cancellation remain unclear, though speculation points to development struggles on other internal projects, potentially pulling resources away from **Ekur**.

## A Shift in Multiplayer Focus

The cancellation of **Project Ekur** raises significant questions about **343 Industries'** long-term strategy for Halo's multiplayer. While **Halo Infinite** continues to receive updates, its player base has struggled to maintain consistent momentum. The potential appeal of a standalone multiplayer title like **Ekur**, which promised larger battles and greater customization, was seen by many as a crucial step in recapturing a broader audience. The project's origins in **Project Tatanka** also suggest a desire to explore different multiplayer formats within the Halo universe, a creative ambition that now appears to be on hold. The loss of **Ekur** leaves a void for fans eager for fresh, large-scale competitive experiences beyond the current offerings.

## What Lies Ahead for Halo?

With **Project Ekur** reportedly shelved, the immediate future of new, distinct multiplayer Halo experiences remains uncertain. While **343 Industries** has not officially commented on the cancellation, the reports suggest a significant setback for a project that held considerable promise. It is unclear if **Ekur** could be revived in the future, especially given Microsoft's stated interest in breathing new life into its flagship franchises. For now, fans will likely continue to engage with **Halo Infinite**, hoping for future content that reignites the passion for the iconic sci-fi shooter's multiplayer modes. Details regarding any potential revival or alternative multiplayer projects have not yet been announced.

content_raw: A brand new Halo multiplayer game has been scrapped, according to sources. A popular Halo YouTuber known as Rebs Gaming has reported that a new multiplayer project set in the beloved sci-fi universe was recently cancelled. This report was also backed up by Windows Central's Jez Corden , who stated that the news was "100% true." The new game was codenamed 'Ekur,' and was being worked on by Certain Affinity, a studio that has done a lot of support work on previous Halo and Call of Duty titles. The game's origins began in a totally different project known as 'Tatanka,' which was a battle royale-esque Halo game. However, that was scrapped in favor of Ekur, which was described as a "super big team battle idea," pulling from Halo's history of large-scale multiplayer modes. Halo 5's Warzone mode was seen as a source of inspiration, as well, and the team also toyed with an extraction mode. The project would've used the map that was built for Tatanka and was being developed in Unreal Engine, not unlike the upcoming Halo: Combat Evolved remake . It's unclear if the goal was to make a multiplayer Halo game that had a broader appeal after Infinite failed to capture a consistent audience, or if it would've been a premium title. Nevertheless, the project supposedly met its end after development troubles on Campaign Evolved, which pulled staff away from the multiplayer project. Whether this game ever sees the light of day is totally up in the air. It's possible it could be revived, especially as Microsoft is trying to inject some life into its biggest franchises right now . It doesn't seem like this was canned as a result of the recent Xbox reset , so hopefully it can find its way back. Although Halo Infinite's servers remain active, the game's player base isn't very lively. It seems hard to imagine that Microsoft would want to keep Halo's multiplayer benched for the foreseeable future, especially with a new Xbox console on the horizon. Campaign Evolved is, as the title implies, a single-player game with the option of co-op. But for those craving a competitive PVP multiplayer experience, they'll have to wait a while. Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.
